definition: A peak experience is a short-lasting, intense state of self-transcendence that some meditation practices aim to bring about. In this context, it is contrasted with a calmer, more enduring “plateau experience.”

reasons: The packet does not explicitly support that a peak experience is “short-lasting” or “intense”; it only contrasts peak experiences with plateau experiences as more calm/persistent (with plateau described as effects lasting at least 1 year).

The packet supports that peak experiences are linked to altered self-transcendence and are an aim/goal of some meditation techniques, but the added specifics about duration and intensity are unsupported by the provided text.

The packet supports that many traditional meditation techniques aim at peak experiences, but it does not directly support defining a peak experience itself as a “short-lasting, intense state of self-transcendence.”

The comparison with a calmer, more enduring “plateau experience” is only partly supported; the packet says plateau experiences are more calm and persistent, but it does not present this as a formal definitional contrast for peak experience.
